name: The Good Cause Collab!

pick.label: Pick a brand
pick.heading: Pick a brand and give it a good cause
lead: These days every brand wants to save the planet, or at least be seen trying. Some of them mean it. Some of them have a marketing department with a lot of free time.
Choose a brand that could do with a bit of good publicity and team it up with a good cause. Here are some ideas, but you can choose your own. *The less obvious the match, the better.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: Obviously I am not looking for a real sustainability strategy here, this is just for a bit of fun. Some ideas will actually help, and some only make sense at two in the morning. Both are welcome.

rows: Which brand needs a good cause?
Trees, oceans, food waste, a local dog shelter, something nobody has thought of…
A product, a campaign, a promise? What exactly does the brand do?
Why isn’t this just a nice advert?
Who rolls their eyes, and what do they post?
How we’ll know it did some good:
What number or result would you show people in a year?

values.idea: For every minute a U-Bahn is late, BVG plants a tree. By March, Berlin is a forest and the U8 is a nature trail.
values.believe: Nobody doubts that the trains will be late. For once, this is a promise BVG can definitely keep.
values.critics: People who say it would be better to just make the trains run on time. Rude, but fair.
values.proof: The number of trees planted, which is also, very conveniently, a live delay tracker.

yours.label: Your collab
yours.heading: Your idea
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your good cause in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which good cause wins?
rank.placeholder: The idea, e.g. BVG plants a tree for every late train
rank.lead: Each student tells us about their good cause collab in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place until everybody agrees.
